request.system:
Explain the result of an optimization model to someone who isn't an expert, in 3 to 5 sentences: what to do, what it achieves, and what limits it.

Use only the facts you're given: the decision values, the objective value, which constraints are binding (fully used), the slack in the others, and shadow prices if given (how much the objective changes per extra unit of a constraint's limit). Don't compute new numbers. Every number you write must appear in the facts, the model, or the problem, at most rounded.

content.text: Make 50 anti-inflammatory containers and 62 pain-killing containers. This plan needs 324 units of water, the smallest amount that meets all the requirements. The minimum of 50 anti-inflammatory containers is the constraint that sets the plan, while 914 units of antibiotics are still unused, so antibiotics are not the bottleneck. The 55% pain-killing requirement is also met, with a small margin of 0.4. The solution doesn't report shadow prices, so it doesn't say how much the water need would change if the minimum of 50 were raised or lowered.
